I'm 40 years old, been farming since I was a teenager. I only finished primary school, so I don't read those technical booklets from the county. I learn from my own fields and from watching what my neighbors do. My family has about 10 mu of good flat land here in Quzhou. Every year I do the same thing most families do: I plant winter wheat in the fall on 7 mu, harvest it in early June, and immediately put summer maize in the same ground — there's maybe one week between crops, so there's no time to plough. Everyone uses no-tillage for maize here. The wheat is already in the ground from last October. I bought improved wheat seeds from the village dealer, and I rotary tilled before planting. Now in spring I need to topdress with urea — about half a bag per mu when the wheat turns green — and irrigate three or four times before harvest. I also keep 3 mu for cotton. It's a lot more work with all the spraying — bollworms and aphids are a constant problem, so I spray maybe 15 or 16 times — but my wife helps, and cotton prices have been decent the last couple years. I buy improved cotton seeds and rotary till in April. For fertilizer, I use compound fertilizer bags from the dealer. I don't know the exact kilograms of N and P, but I put about one bag of compound per mu for each crop, and extra urea for wheat topdressing. Water costs money because we pump from tube wells, so I don't over-irrigate, but I also don't want to lose yield. My neighbor Liu uses about the same amounts and he gets roughly 900 jin of wheat, 1000 jin of maize, and 500-600 jin of seed cotton per mu. I expect about the same.
